 Ja'Kobi Lane More Intriguing With New QB in Town 
 0m Link copied! 
 Share: 
 Link copied to clipboard! 
 See RotoBaller at 
 the top of Google 
 Nov 16, 2026, 6:47 PM ET 
Despite not drawing a single target in the Thursday night blowout loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 9, Baltimore Ravens rookie wide receiver Ja'Kobi Lane has become more intriguing off the waiver wire heading into the Monday night contest against the winless Los Angeles Chargers to close out Week 10 action. The 22-year-old had the third-most offensive snaps (32) against the Jaguars behind Zay Flowers and Rashod Bateman , but he did not draw a single look from undrafted rookie quarterback Joe Fagnano , who was making his first career start with both Lamar Jackson (thumb) and Tyler Huntley (toe) on Injured Reserve. Lane was drawing rave reviews in training camp this summer and was setting himself up to take over the No. 2 WR role in Baltimore from Bateman before missing time with an injury. Between his injury and injuries to Jackson at QB, Lane has failed to get off the ground in his first five games in the NFL, catching only nine of 14 targets for 89 yards. He is still searching for his first trip to paydirt. Most of Lane's fantasy appeal in 2026 is as a dynasty/keeper stash, but with veteran QB Jacoby Brissett now in town and set to take over as the Ravens' starter under center on Monday night against the Chargers, Lane's single-league fantasy value may not be completely lost. He is a deep-league flier off the waiver wire and is currently only rostered in 7% of Yahoo leagues. -- Keith Hernandez 
 Source: Pro Football Reference

The Philadelphia Eagles designated running back Will Shipley (foot) to return from Injured Reserve by opening his 21-day practice window on Monday, according to Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Sports. Shipley suffered a partial tear of his plantar fascia in the team's Week 5 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars and has been on IR ever since, but if he looks good in practice this week, he could have a chance to be officially activated and play this Sunday in Week 11 against the visiting Pittsburgh Steelers. Tank Bigsby (abdomen) also remains on IR, but if Shipley is activated before Bigsby, he would be in line to serve as the direct backup to starter Saquon Barkley , potentially making him a desperation flex option in the deepest of PPR fantasy football leagues. The 24-year-old Shipley, a fourth-rounder in 2024 from Clemson, had 20 rushing attempts for only 57 yards (2.9 yards per carry) and one touchdown in the first five games of the year, adding five catches on his eight targets for 31 yards in the passing game. Right now, Barkley is the only RB the Eagles have on their active roster, with Elijah Mitchell and Jaydon Blue on the practice squad. Mitchell had a season-high 11 carries for 34 yards on Nov. 1 against the division-rival Washington Commanders with Barkley battling hamstring and back issues, but he had just three carries for six yards and three catches for 20 yards in the Week 9 loss to the division-rival New York Giants. -- Keith Hernandez

The New York Giants had veteran running back Antonio Gibson in for a workout on Monday, according to Ari Meirov of The 33rd Team. When asked if he and general manager Andrew Berry have had a discussion about quarterback Deshaun Watson 's future in Cleveland on Monday, Browns head coach Todd Monken said they "have not," according to Daniel Oyefusi of ESPN. "That's a question really for Andrew, but we have not had discussions about really most of our roster, we have not had discussions about moving forward," Monken added. The 31-year-old Watson has not been perfect by any stretch in his return to action in 2026 following a torn Achilles that caused him to miss all of last year, but he has gone 6-3 in his nine starts, throwing for 2,118 yards, seven touchdowns, and four interceptions. Watson has been a middling QB2 option in superflex fantasy leagues; he has not thrown a touchdown in the last four games, and he also leads the NFL with 37 sacks taken, but he led another inspiring comeback win over the Houston Texans in Week 10. The five-year, $230 million contract that the Browns signed him to in March of 2022 has been a massive overpay for a player who did not play over seven games from 2022 through 2025, and it is still unlikely at this point that he will factor into the organization's future. For now, he remains the Browns' starter going into their Week 11 bye, but if the wheels fall off at any point, Monken might not hesitate to throw Shedeur Sanders in there for more upside. -- Keith Hernandez
